Definition: from G288 and G2041; a vine-worker, i.e. pruner:--vine-dresser.
BiblicalUsage: The word appears once, in the parable of the fig tree: the owner tells the dresser of his vineyard that for three years he has come seeking fruit and found none, and the tree should be cut down, since it only cumbers the ground. The vinedresser is the one who tends the planting and speaks for it — and in the next verse he asks for one more year to dig about it and dung it.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a gardener carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the parable's patience — one more year, one more chance to bear fruit.
